# Chang Chung-yuan — *Tao: A New Way of Thinking* (2014)

[Source index](../../../README.md) · [Reading entrance](../../../../../../README.md) · [48 movements](../../../../../../section-rooms/README.md)

## Bibliographic identity

The work is Chang Chung-yuan's translation of the Tao Tê Ching with an introduction and chapter-by-chapter commentaries. Chang (1907–1988), Professor of Philosophy at the University of Hawaiʻi at Mānoa and author of *Creativity and Taoism*, reads each chapter beside Western metaphysics — Heidegger above all, with Hegel, Schopenhauer, Jung, Plato, Kant, and Nietzsche named by the publisher; the chapters Frank read also quote Nishida.

The selected edition is the Singing Dragon reprint, published 21 January 2014, 240 pages, ISBN 978-1-84819-201-0. Singing Dragon is an imprint of Jessica Kingsley Publishers (London and Philadelphia); the publisher's product record verifies title, subtitle, format, extent, date, and ISBN. The work was first published in 1975 by Harper & Row (New York). Title renderings vary across records — the publisher prints "Tao – A New Way of Thinking" over the subtitle "A Translation of the Tao Tê Ching with an Introduction and Commentaries," while library records give "Tao, a new way of thinking" — and the Chicago forms below join the double subtitle in the standard way.

Frank's encounter notes cite pp. 83–93, covering the commentaries to chapters 20 through 22. Those locators are presumed to track the 2014 pagination of the copy at hand; collating them against the physical copy is the open verification step, and if the copy proves to be the 1975 printing the house's selected edition should be re-decided rather than silently repaginated.

The sibling `chung-yuan-chang-tao-a-new-way-of-thinking-2014-NOTES.md` is Frank G. Taylor's authorial encounter with the work. It was read in full for the present source work and remains untouched; its copied passages are leads until verified against the selected edition.

## Source scholarship

Chang's operation is that of a philosopher-translator: he renders the Tao Tê Ching so that its ontology can be heard within Western metaphysics, and his commentaries stage direct meetings — Heidegger's claim that the Nothing is more original than the Not and negation, the region as the open cleared by the primal conflict of opposites, and the passage in *On the Way to Language* where Heidegger ventures that Tao could be the way that gives all ways; Jung on the identity of opposites from *Psychological Types* and on the unconscious as worldly and objective in scope; Nishida on the union of subject and object as the point where religion and morality are exhausted. Chapter 20's commentary distinguishes the self-identity of contradictions as lived in actual life from any unification of opposites achieved through intellection; chapter 21's turns on Tao as indistinct and ineffable yet containing all forms, the creativity that is the source of all things.

Frank's encounter-intent, recovered from `chung-yuan-chang-tao-a-new-way-of-thinking-2014-NOTES.md` and named here as his and only his: he maps the lived self-identity of contradictions to `0/1` and the intellectual synthesis to `4+2`, with the MEF lenses giving the synthesis its real meta-epistemic standing; he adds the dia-ballein failure mode — one-sided calculative thought as the misapprehension of the original identity of opposites — as the project's own extension, flagged as such in the notes and carrying the mythic register of the fall deliberately; he hears Heidegger's priority of the Nothing as the exact shape of Zero's priority to the `(−1)` of cancellation; he reads Tao's indistinctness-containing-all-forms as Mono/Poly, the `0/1` and `1/0`; he takes Heidegger's Tao passage as a pointer to Epi-Logos, logos returning to the Saying prior to the said; and he links Chang's creativity to Whitehead's, with QL as the archetypal form of concrescence and the `0/1`–`1/0` pair as Spanda. His note registers the encounter's force: he finds the whole `(0/1)/(1/0)` self-identity effort to be about Tao.

Claim boundary: Chang translates and comments; he formulates neither QL, nor the dia-ballein/sym-ballein pair, nor the Spanda equations. The evidential relation for each mapping is Argued from or Resonant with, to be fixed passage by passage at verification. Chang's commentary deepens and tests the two-logics fulcrum and the Zero thread; it does not derive them.

Nested-quotation warning: the passages Frank copied include Chang quoting Nishida, Jung (*Psychological Types*), and Heidegger (*Existence and Being*; *On the Way to Language*). Until each is collated in its own primary edition, any such wording is double transmission through Chang and may be attributed only as "quoted by Chang," on the same pattern as the Watson–Gans chain in `watson-1998-resonance-of-emptiness`.

## Essay uses

Encounter-intent leads only; no canonical consumer is declared yet, and `consumed_by_sections` / `consumed_by_arguments` remain empty until real consumption is wired. Candidate destinations from the notes: the two-logics fulcrum (lived identity of opposites beside intellectual synthesis, with dia-ballein as the traced failure mode); the priority of Zero over negation and cancellation; Mono/Poly and the `0/1`–`1/0` self-identity work; the Epi-Logos naming through Heidegger's Tao passage; and the convergence Frank observes among Jung, Whitehead, Heidegger, and Gebser around a Taoist ontology of the ever-present origin.

## Passages and excerpts

No passage cards yet. `chung-yuan-chang-tao-a-new-way-of-thinking-2014-NOTES.md` carries quotation leads at pp. 83–93 (2014 pagination presumed): the Nishida passages on true self and subject–object union (p. 83); chapter 20's commentary on the self-identity of contradictions (p. 84); the Jung *Psychological Types* and unconscious passages (pp. 85–86); the region (p. 87); the Heidegger Nothing passages and Chang's Tao comparison (p. 89); the *On the Way to Language* Tao passage (p. 90); the indistinct-form and liberation-from-delusion passages (pp. 90–91); chapter 22 on the wise identifying opposites as one (p. 92); and the motion–quiescence passage with Chang's Hegel and Nishida comparisons (p. 93), which Frank's notes tie to Spanda and to completing a dialectical logic of concrescence. Each lead is `unverified` until transcribed and collated against the selected edition; the nested Nishida, Jung, and Heidegger wordings additionally require collation in their own primary editions before attribution beyond "quoted by Chang." No wording from `chung-yuan-chang-tao-a-new-way-of-thinking-2014-NOTES.md` may be printed as quotation.
